The test image shows a corn ear with husks pulled back. The kernels are mostly yellow/golden with some slight discoloration. The husks have a notable pinkish tint. No obvious heavy mold growth visible. This is a seed/pod image.

Top candidates from the seed/pod classes: Gibberella_Disease (pink mold), Fusarium_Disease (whitish-pink), Diplodia_Ear_Rot (white mycelium from base), Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, Aspergillus_Ear_Rot. Let me also consider less obvious options.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with my top candidates.
Gibberella reference shows clear red/pink mold at the ear tip with darkened kernels. The test image doesn't match this pattern. Let me check Fusarium.
Fusarium shows whitish fungal growth on scattered kernels. The test image has some subtle discoloration but not the clear white cottony growth. Let me check Diplodia Ear Rot.
Diplodia shows severely rotted, grayish-brown kernels. Not matching. Let me check Trichoderma.
Trichoderma shows dark blue-green/black mold on kernels. Not matching. Let me check Aspergillus Ear Rot.

None of the heavily molded references match. The test image shows a relatively clean ear with pinkish husks and subtle kernel discoloration. Let me check the Gibberella pod reference and Diplodia pod reference for milder presentations.
This is a strong match. The Gibberella pod reference shows husks with pinkish-reddish discoloration, very similar to the test image's pinkish husks. Let me check Diplodia pod for comparison.
Diplodia shows bleached/brown husks, not the pinkish tint of the test image. Let me view one more Gibberella reference to confirm.

This Gibberella reference also shows pinkish discoloration on husks in the background, consistent with the disease pattern.

**Analysis summary:**

The test image shows a corn ear with:
- Distinctly **pinkish/reddish husks** (the most prominent diagnostic feature)
- Mostly intact golden kernels with subtle discoloration
- No heavy mold coverage

Comparing across references:
- **Gibberella_Disease pod reference** (Corn_Disease_64.jpg) was the strongest match, showing the same pinkish-reddish husk discoloration
- **Aspergillus, Trichoderma** showed heavy green/dark mold, not matching
- **Diplodia** showed bleached/brown husks, not pink
- **Fusarium** showed white cottony growth on kernels, not present here

The KB confirms: Gibberella causes "red or pink colored mold... pink mold is visible on the outside of the husks at the ear tip." The pinkish husks are the hallmark.
